newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes little changed against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes little changed against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended almost unchanged at 8.3070 against the U.S. dollar on Monday, from last Friday's 8.3071, on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
Dealers said that the yuan's rise was limited by a cut in bank interest rates last Friday, but it was supported by expectations of a healthy trade surplus for China in the remaining months of 1996.
The yuan opened at 8.3070 and fell slightly to move around 8.3075, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3078 early in the session.
It then rose steadily late in trading, hitting a high of 8.3064 before closing.
Trading was sluggish with most done at about 8.3075, traders said.
"The yuan's upward momentum slowed because demand for the yuan fell as a result of the central bank cutting interest rates last Friday," one dealer said.
"Exports in the third quarter are continuing to grow, so more dollar-selling is expected to support the yuan," another dealer said.
He said that given the conflicting factors, many traders had taken to the sidelines to see how the yuan moves in the short term.
Dealers expected the yuan would continue to move around 8.3070 on Tuesday.
The yuan ended down at 7.7000 from 7.6625 against 100 Japanese yen, and up at 1.0730 from 1.0745 against the Hong Kong dollar.
